title: The Anger in Orbit
retrieval_query: Iliad Book 1 Chryses ransom Apollo plague assembly Calchas Agamemnon Achilles Briseis withdrawal honor supplication
premise: Write the opening movement of an Iliad reimagined in 2526 CE, five hundred years after the present. Four developed chapters, about 2,800 words altogether. After nine years of blockade, the Achaean coalition besieges Troy, a sovereign orbital habitat above Mars. The physician-priest Chryses seeks the release of his adult daughter Chryseis; Agamemnon refuses, an Apollo-linked epidemic exposes the price of that refusal, and the ensuing council breaks the alliance between Agamemnon and Achilles. End with Achilles withdrawing his Myrmidon carrier from combat duty and seeking Thetis’s intervention, leaving the war unresolved. This must FEEL futuristic in bodies, labor, communications, medicine, habitation, logistics and political power; preserve the Iliad’s causal conflict and epic gravity rather than dressing ancient camps in neon.

length_policy.policy: Exactly four chapters, one developed 700-word scene each. Close this opening movement in chapter four; leave the greater war unresolved. No fifth chapter or endless new subplot.

genre: Futuristic political and military epic; literary science fiction
reader_experience: Immersion in a physically inhabited future; compassion for captives and patients; mounting dread as private humiliation becomes public catastrophe.
pov: Third-person past tense with one primary focal character per chapter. No quoted/direct dialogue, first-person narration, invocation or direct address. Render arguments through specific narrated offers, refusals, actions and consequences. Author knowledge is not shared character knowledge.
tone_mood: Grave, lucid and politically charged. Epic scale grounded in bodily vulnerability; no generic action-film triumph or archaic costume drama.
sensory_detail: Ventilator rhythms, adhesive soles in spin gravity, worn pressure seals, projection lag, heat radiators, recycled air, diagnostic skin patches and the labor that keeps habitats alive.
ending_tendency: Resolve the four-chapter opening arc with a consequential withdrawal, while leaving the siege and divine-political intervention unresolved.

style.narrator: Third-person past tense with one primary focal character per chapter. No quoted/direct dialogue, first-person narration, invocation or direct address. Render arguments through specific narrated offers, refusals, actions and consequences. Author knowledge is not shared character knowledge.
style.register: Elevated but clear contemporary English. Musical variation, exact physical detail, tense subtext and restrained exposition. Epic dignity without faux-archaic filler.
wording: Technology must alter feasible choices and social power; do not merely rename spears and ships.
Use stable names, locations, counts, ownership and deadlines across all chapters.
Avoid stock holograms, neon, quantum jargon, generic AI explanations and repeated eyes/hands gestures.
No quotation or close reproduction of modern translations.

figurative_language.guidance: At most one developed simile per chapter if earned; vary domains across chapters and return to the action. Do not repeat the same demonstration in adjacent writing beats.

style.interiority: Concrete perception, conflicted intention and selective memory; no moral summary after a legible action.
style.dialogue: No direct or quoted speech; preserve distinct bargaining strategies through narrated exchanges.
style.explanation: Reveal future systems through consequential use and failure, without explanatory lectures.

world_rules: The date is 2526 CE. Troy is a sovereign orbital habitat above Mars; the Achaean expedition has maintained a blockade for nine years. No literal Bronze Age camp or newly discovered firearm exists in this universe.
Atreus is Agamemnon’s flagship; Peleus is Achilles’s Myrmidon carrier; Nereid is Odysseus’s medical shuttle. These names, roles and affiliations never change.

Chryseis is an adult physician held under coercive custody aboard Atreus at the opening. Briseis is an adult captive medic aboard Peleus. They are distinct people with agency and separate histories; neither is a payment token or interchangeable daughter.

Apollo is a distributed medical authority with orbital infrastructure and biological consequences; Chryses holds a recognized human priest-physician credential. Denial of Apollo maintenance and quarantine cooperation helps sustain an actual epidemic. Never supply pathogen design, synthesis or dissemination instructions.

Zeus is an inter-habitat arbitration authority; Thetis is a human envoy with access to its treaty channel. Their precise intentions remain uncertain; no omniscient AI, instant cure, resurrection, time travel or magic cancellation of earlier costs.

Habitat air, spin gravity, life-support maintenance, delayed authenticated communications, finite shuttle capacity and custody permissions constrain action. Travel and medical recovery take time. Introduce arrivals before actions and show how a character gains private information.

The Nereid manifest starts with twelve sealed isolation cartridges. Four are consumed stabilizing patients during chapter two; eight remain afterward. No replenishment in this opening. Preserve the count and who witnesses or receives the updated manifest.

Chapter one is blockade day zero for this episode. Chapter two occurs nine days after Chryses’s refusal. Chapter three follows that assembly on the same day; chapter four occurs after a physical escort has had time to reach Peleus.

Achilles’s carrier withdrawal is a refusal of combat duty, not abandonment of his crew, instant escape from Mars or an attack on allied patients. The Trojans do not automatically know private coalition decisions.
No predetermined Greek victory, fall of Troy, deaths of Achilles or Hector, completed intervention by Zeus or resolution of the entire war in these four chapters.

plot_design.central_question: How does a commander’s claim to honor turn a life-support crisis into a rupture of the coalition?
plot_design.arc_question: Will evidence and supplication produce restitution, or will Agamemnon make another person pay for his concession?
causal_dependencies: Chryses offers ransom and medical cooperation; Agamemnon refuses publicly.
Nine days of epidemic expose the dependency on Apollo cooperation; Calchas needs Achilles’s protection to name it.
Agamemnon agrees to return Chryseis but claims Briseis in compensation; Achilles cannot erase that coercion through superior weapons.
A physical transfer changes custody; Achilles withdraws combat service and seeks Thetis’s intervention, opening the larger epic.

subplots.question: Who bears the cost of keeping the sick alive when commanders trade human freedom?
subplots.independent_action: Use finite isolation cartridges to evacuate patients.
subplots.intersection: The reduced supply makes the quarrel’s practical cost visible.
subplots.removal_cost: Without patients and finite transport the quarrel risks becoming abstract honor talk.

alternatives_and_costs: Concede the ransom without compensation and risk public authority.
Protect standing by imposing a new coercive transfer and lose the strongest carrier’s service.
plot_design.local_resolution: The opening rupture occurs; no victory or repaired alliance.
unresolved: The fate of the siege, Briseis’s autonomy, Thetis’s petition and the epidemic’s recovery.

chapter_arcs: Chryses offers ransom and Apollo maintenance cooperation aboard Atreus; Agamemnon publicly refuses release of Chryseis. Chryses leaves with his credential intact. No plague explanation or future quarrel yet.

Nine days later the sick overwhelm quarantine. Odysseus spends four of Nereid’s twelve isolation cartridges, leaving eight, and reports the manifest. Achilles protects Calchas so the diagnostician can identify the blocked Apollo cooperation and demand Chryseis’s return. No Briseis transfer yet.

In the same council, Agamemnon concedes Chryseis’s return via Nereid but orders Briseis taken from Peleus in compensation. Achilles chooses not to attack fellow crews and announces withdrawal of combat duty. Show the political threat as an enforceable custody order; do not yet enact the later escort arrival.

After transit, the escort takes Briseis from Peleus; she acts to protect her patients and states terms through narrated action. Achilles disables his combat authorization while preserving life support, and contacts Thetis. She agrees only to carry his petition through Zeus’s treaty channel. End on the tangible cost and unresolved petition; no granted victory.

Wrath, supplication, contested honor and costly withdrawal

initial_facts.text: The date is 2526 CE. After nine years of blockade, Troy habitat above Mars remains independent. Atreus belongs to Agamemnon; Peleus to Achilles; Nereid is Odysseus’s medical shuttle.
Chryseis is held aboard Atreus; Briseis is a distinct adult captive medic aboard Peleus. Neither has been transferred at the opening.
Nereid carries twelve sealed isolation cartridges at the opening. No cartridge has yet been consumed in this episode.
Chryses has a recognized Apollo physician-priest credential and seeks the release of his daughter Chryseis. Thetis has access to Zeus’s arbitration channel.

must_avoid: Ancient camps, bronze weapon fetish, neon wallpaper or unexplained quantum jargon.
Instant travel, magical cures, knowledge of future scenes, inconsistent ship names or cartridge counts.
Treating captive women as interchangeable prizes without agency.
Repeated setup, repeated demonstrations, repeated similes or moral explanations of already legible action.
Modern translation quotations or close imitation.
Ending the whole war or extending beyond the four-chapter opening.
quality_contract: Four distinct developed chapters, about 700 words each, in order. No direct dialogue or headings inside generated prose.
Technology and material constraints drive choices. Every chapter must feel inhabited and futuristic, not simply decorated.
Maintain exact identity, location, time, custody, resource arithmetic and individual knowledge across chapters and writing batches.
Distinguish ancient source influence from the binding futuristic author brief.
Give women agency, commanders conflicting aims, and choices irreversible human costs.
Use varied concrete language; no duplicate paragraphs, repeated decisive actions or unexplained character entrances.
Conclude this opening with withdrawal and a pending petition, leaving the greater war unresolved.

chapter_contract.arc: Complete this chapter’s assigned irreversible development without repeating earlier discoveries or executing later chapters.
chapter_contract.continuity: Check the actual preceding prose and source-bound facts, fixed carrier identities, captives’ custody, elapsed time, and twelve minus four equals eight isolation cartridges.
chapter_contract.ending: Chapter four completes the opening rupture; no chapter five, immediate Zeus resolution or fall of Troy.
